prompt:
Write a clinical treatment summary (about 150 words) by the treating provider for a patient with whiplash after a low-speed head-on collision. The patient had 10 visits. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1016; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Imaging and exam findings clearly confirm the injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- The bills show no repeated charges.
text:
The patient presented following a low-speed head-on collision with complaints of neck pain, stiffness, and headache consistent with whiplash-type cervical injury. The mechanism of injury is well matched to the reported symptoms, and the clinical picture reflects the kind and force of the impact. Physical examination documented restricted cervical range of motion and paraspinal muscle tenderness, and imaging findings clearly confirm the soft tissue injury to the neck. No prior injury to the cervical spine is known from the patient's history or available records.

Care was delivered over ten visits and followed a typical course for this type of injury, consisting of manual therapy, supervised therapeutic exercise, and a home stretching program. Symptoms improved steadily, with pain scores and range of motion gradually returning toward baseline, and visit frequency was tapered accordingly as recovery progressed. Billing records reflect single, appropriate charges for each service rendered with no repeated or duplicate entries.

At the most recent evaluation the patient reported substantial improvement and near-resolution of symptoms. Discharge to a self-directed home program is recommended, with return precautions provided should neck pain or neurological symptoms recur.
